purpose: Per-fact evidence for pack.json (CMP-029). pack.schema.json has no per-fact evidence field and caps notes at 500 characters, so sources live here. Labels: VERIFIED-OFFICIAL (official source read, per the cited repo doc), SECONDARY (treat as UNVERIFIED), UNVERIFIED, PLATFORM-DEFAULT (a platform choice, not a statutory claim). Access dates are those recorded in the cited repo doc; no source was re-read in this session. A source not read in full (a snippet or not fetched) carries read: false and no access date. NOT legal advice.

facts.claim: No UAE chart of accounts exists yet. The reference is pending and the pack must not be used for a tenant until a reviewed chart is registered.
VAT applies in the UAE (5%). No UAE tax codes exist yet, so taxCodesRef is pending and finance.vat_ae_treatments is a placeholder (goLiveBlockers); the pack holds no rate.

sources.note: snippets of official pages only, per country-matrix.md row U5 (research of 2026-11-04)

facts.claim: VAT returns are usually quarterly and monthly where the FTA assigns it. Filing frequency was not confirmed.
Commercial rounding, half away from zero, so credit notes mirror invoices. A founder decision, not an FTA rule.
A Tax Registration Number (TRN) has 15 digits, as the Blueprint contract already assumes.
There is no single national trade licence number format: each emirate and free zone issues its own. The pattern is deliberately permissive (letters, digits, slash and hyphen, up to 30).

The UAE model is DCTCE (Peppol five-corner): the supplier sends PINT AE data to its accredited service provider (ASP), which reports onward. The mode id uae_e_invoicing is the Blueprint contract value, itself a placeholder id.
The Ministry of Finance runs the programme (read). That the FTA is Corner 5, the tax authority that receives the reports, is an inference, so naming both is UNVERIFIED.
facts.sourceNote: The PINT AE page (https://docs.peppol.eu/poac/ae/pint-ae/, provider-selection item 9) was removed as a source here: it backs neither item 1 nor item 3 (review of #267). It still backs eInvoicing.mode.

facts.claim: Pack 0.1.0 marks e-invoicing not yet required because no go-live date has passed, but it is required for businesses with revenue of AED 50 million or more from 2027-01-01 (goLiveBlockers uae_e_invoicing); smaller businesses by 2027-07-01 (unverified). No UAE e-invoicing component exists until CMP-011, so compliance.pint_ae is a placeholder id. The pack computes no threshold.

sources.note: AED 50 million band dates, VERIFIED in the cited doc

facts.claim: No language requirement for UAE e-invoices was found, so none is declared.

No official source says any language is mandatory on a UAE tax invoice; it is often cited as not mandatory. The schema needs at least one language, so the minimal list is Arabic (Arabic first, principle 4). English is a template option, not locked.

Five years for VAT records is commonly cited (longer for real estate and corporate tax). No source was read. The number is locked but UNVERIFIED; the retention for the ASP copy and ours is open (Q-213).
The UAE uses one time zone, the IANA zone Asia/Dubai. The loader checks that the zone exists; no official source was read.
Commerce and tax use the Gregorian calendar and no Hijri requirement was found, so no second date is shown by default. The Hijri format is kept only because the schema requires it.
Most employers keep a Saturday and Sunday weekend and a Monday to Friday week after the 2022 change; government Fridays are partial. Companies can override it.
facts.ref: docs/architecture/calendars-and-locale.md section Week, weekend and working time

facts.claim: 08:00 to 17:00 is a platform default that companies override. The statutory limits in Federal Decree-Law 33 of 2021 were not read.
Private-sector hours are reported to be two hours shorter in Ramadan (08:00 to 15:00 here). Not read.
Gregorian year from 1 January is a platform default; companies may move the start month. A Hijri fiscal year is not offered in the UAE pack (no Hijri use found, U17).
facts.ref: docs/architecture/calendars-and-locale.md section Fiscal year and periods

facts.claim: Holidays come from the ae.holidays calendar, which CMP-024 builds; it does not exist yet. The pack holds no holiday dates.
Western digits, a dot for decimals, a comma for thousands and day/month/year dates are platform display defaults; the user can switch to Eastern Arabic digits.
The currency is the UAE dirham (ISO 4217 AED) with two decimals. ISO 4217 was not read.
Payroll, WPS (SIF files) and gratuity are off: payroll is out of v1 scope and arrives with CMP-015 (gate G3). The underlying rules are unread.
No UAE tax invoice mode exists: the neutral layout refuses UAE invoices (Q-553). The template and its component are pending CMP-011. The legal layout always wins over tenant branding.

sources.note: Cabinet Decision 52 of 2017 Art. 59(1), cited UNVERIFIED in the ERP-016 print formats
